    Interactive MSSR explorer

    Source: R/app.R
    mssr_app.Rd

    Opens a Shiny app for trying mssr() on synthetic examples or on an uploaded frame. It shows the input and the structure map side by side on the same input-pixel axes, line profiles, structural masks applied to the original data (mssr_mask()) and the fixture self-test (mssr_selftest()), and offers the structure map, the mask, a figure and a run record for download. The app calls the exported functions, so its results are the same as in R; it adds no processing of its own.

    Usage

    mssr_app(max_upload_mb = 50, ...)

    Arguments

    max_upload_mb

    Maximum upload size in megabytes.

    ...

    Passed to shiny::runApp(), for example port or launch.browser.

    Value

    The value of shiny::runApp(), invisibly; called for its side effect.

    Details

    Uploads. Delimited text (.csv comma-separated, .tsv or .txt separated by tabs or spaces; numbers only, no header), PNG (needs the png package; values as returned by png::readPNG(), scaled to 0..1) and TIFF (needs the tiff package; stored values, unscaled). Multi-channel images are not converted to gray: choose one channel. For multi-page TIFF choose a page. Files are read by the R process that runs the app (your own session when started with mssr_app()); the app sends nothing elsewhere. Run records include SHA-256 identities of uploaded bytes and decoded matrix content (needs digest). Source filenames and paths are excluded. Retain the original input and preprocessing separately; a digest identifies content, not acquisition authenticity. Compare a retained file with digest::digest(file = path, algo = "sha256", serialize = FALSE).

    Limits. To keep the app responsive, runs whose estimated work exceeds 5e8 operations are refused; call mssr() directly for larger runs. The image header is checked before decoding; image uploads are limited to 5e7 samples, conservatively allowing at least four channels per pixel. Only the selected TIFF page is decoded. Integer TIFF samples keep their stored values; floating-point TIFF samples remain unscaled. The structure map is not a quantitative intensity, and nothing in the app implies a gain in physical resolution. Packed 12-bit, signed-integer, palette, multi-channel planar-separate and volumetric TIFF images are unsupported; prepare an explicit supported 2D frame before uploading. The TIFF preflight accepts classic TIFF, top-left orientation, grayscale black-is-zero or RGB samples, at most 256 pages, 4096 tags per page, 4 MiB of directory/tag metadata and a 256 MiB file. BigTIFF, nested directories and other orientations/color conversions are refused. These are workload guards, not a hard decoder memory or time guarantee. Computation runs in one background R process per app session (needs callr). Cancel stops only that session's job. Incomplete results cannot be downloaded; the previous completed result can be explicitly restored. A job is cancelled when its session closes or after five minutes. The child inherits CPU affinity and uses one numerical thread. Changed settings are marked stale; downloads retain the computed input and settings. Development-source launches also need pkgload. A job is refused when package files, functions or the native library differ from what the R session loaded, instead of running other code.

    Examples

    if (interactive()) {
  mssr_app()
}
